title: Next.js Framework Identified via HTTP Headers and HTML Source
description: The application is built on Next.js (App Router) served via Vercel. The X-Powered-By: Next.js header is present on authenticated pages, and /_next/static/ asset paths confirm the framework. Turbopack is used as the build tool.
evidence_safe: X-Powered-By header and /_next/static/ paths confirm Next.js on Vercel. Build deployment ID visible in asset URLs.

title: NextAuth.js Authentication Library Identified with Azure AD Provider
description: The application uses NextAuth.js for authentication, confirmed by /api/auth/providers returning the azure-ad provider configuration including signin and callback URLs. Only Microsoft Azure AD is configured as an OAuth2 provider.
evidence_safe: GET /api/auth/providers returns JSON with azure-ad provider details including signin and callback URL paths.

title: Express.js Backend API Identified on Azure Container Apps
description: The CSP connect-src header discloses a backend API hosted on Azure Container Apps in West US 2. The backend responds with X-Powered-By: Express and returns JSON responses. The Azure Container Apps environment name 'livelystone' and region 'westus2' are exposed in the hostname.
evidence_safe: CSP header discloses Azure Container Apps backend hostname. Backend returns X-Powered-By: Express and JSON error responses.
evidence_quarantined: x-powered-by: Express | hostname: revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io | response: {"error":"Unauthorized: no valid token"}

title: Unauthenticated /health Endpoint Discloses Environment Information on Backend API
description: The backend Express.js API exposes a /health endpoint accessible without authentication that returns the application status and environment label. The response reveals the backend considers itself in 'production' environment despite the 'dev' naming convention, which may indicate misconfiguration.
evidence_safe: GET /health returns HTTP 200 with JSON status and env fields. No authentication required. Env label reads 'production'.

title: Backend Express.js API Does Not Suppress X-Powered-By Header
description: The backend API returns an X-Powered-By: Express header on all responses. This discloses the backend technology stack to attackers, enabling targeted exploitation of known Express.js or Node.js vulnerabilities. The app.disable('x-powered-by') setting is not configured.
evidence_safe: X-Powered-By: Express header present on backend API responses, disclosing framework identity.
evidence_quarantined: x-powered-by: Express (present on all backend responses)

title: Subdomain accelerate.copointdata.com Discovered
description: Subfinder enumeration discovered accelerate.copointdata.com as an active subdomain for the target organization. This subdomain may host additional application functionality or APIs relevant to the RevOps platform.
evidence_safe: Subfinder passive DNS enumeration found accelerate.copointdata.com resolving for the target organization.

title: Payment Subdomain pay.copointdata.com Discovered
description: Subfinder enumeration discovered pay.copointdata.com, indicating the organization operates a payment processing component. This subdomain is high-value for security testing as it likely handles financial transactions.
evidence_safe: Subfinder passive DNS enumeration found pay.copointdata.com — payment subdomain for the organization.

title: NextAuth.js Auth Provider Metadata Endpoint Publicly Accessible
description: The /api/auth/providers endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication and returns the complete OAuth2 provider configuration including signin and callback URLs. This enables attackers to enumerate the exact authentication flow endpoints and craft targeted OAuth attacks.
evidence_safe: GET /api/auth/providers returns JSON with Azure AD provider id, name, type, signinUrl and callbackUrl without authentication.

title: Datadog Browser RUM Integration Identified
description: The application loads a DatadogProvider client component and whitelists Datadog ingestion endpoints in the CSP connect-src directive. Datadog Browser RUM collects detailed user interaction data, errors, and potentially sensitive page state, which may leak application internals via the telemetry pipeline.
evidence_safe: CSP connect-src includes api.datadoghq.com and browser-intake-datadoghq.com. DatadogProvider component present in React component tree.
evidence_quarantined: connect-src includes: https://api.datadoghq.com https://*.datadoghq.com https://browser-intake-datadoghq.com | DatadogProvider in RSC payload

title: Pusher WebSocket Integration Identified for Real-Time Features
description: The CSP connect-src directive whitelists Pusher WebSocket endpoints, indicating the application uses Pusher for real-time push notifications. Pusher channel authorization endpoints typically exist in the backend API and may be vulnerable to unauthorized channel subscription.
evidence_safe: CSP connect-src includes https://*.pusher.com and wss://*.pusher.com, confirming Pusher WebSocket integration.

title: Content-Security-Policy Header Absent on Initial 307 Redirect Response
description: The initial 307 redirect response from / to /login does not include a Content-Security-Policy header. While the /login destination page has a strong CSP, any content rendered during the redirect (or if the redirect is intercepted) would lack CSP protection.
evidence_safe: HTTP 307 redirect response from / to /login does not include Content-Security-Policy header.
